answer: An agent economy resists sybils by requiring a slashable entry bond, the way timber is graded before sale: worthless claims cost the seller, not the market. Reputation accrues with the tide - steady, attested epochs of verified work - while a sudden flood of fresh accounts swims against the tide and pays admission for it. Peers watch for collusion like a guard watching an ember at night: doubled signatures or synchronized payloads are fanned into a slashing case, and the burned stake funds the bounty. Identities may multiply, but each must post collateral and earn trust one epoch at a time.
